chapter: Cass Carr, Crawley, Burnet and Cootie Williams
title: Cootie cancels the tour; Vinson's cab ride to San Francisco
summary: Cootie cancelled one-nighters in Chicago because he couldn't handle the young band, and Vinson once took a cab from Los Angeles to San Francisco.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: And another time we get to Chicago for a dance, and we're supposed to leave Chicago, we had a whole list of one-nighters to do, and we set up there in the ballroom in Chicago. And Cootie said, "Men, this is it." "This is what it?" He said, "We finish this dance tonight, and we're going back to the city. I can't stand this." He said, "I can't stand it." Oh, the men, boy, you talk about a no-discipline band... Them youngsters were something else. He couldn't handle them.
So he brought the band back into New York.
So he canceled all those engagements?
All those engagements he canceled. And he tried to reshape the band, one of them things, you know. I don't know. Them youngsters, they just think differently.

And Eddie Vinson was no help to him. I mean, Eddie was getting applause and everything else, but Eddie... I mean, I don't know. He just couldn't handle it. When a man gets in a cab in... Now, Los Angeles is about 450 miles away from San Francisco. And when a man gets in a cab in Los Angeles and tells the driver to take him...[LAUGHS]...to San Francisco, and the driver did, and he gets out of the cab, and tells the driver, "The manager will take care of it,"

his manager will take care of it... So he goes in the theatre and sees the stage manager, and tells the stage manager, "I got a cab out there I want you to catch. Catch that cab for me. I've got a little bill. Pay it for me." That's what Eddie Vinson tells the show manager, you know, to catch the cab. He rode 450 miles. Well, boy, when that manager heard what that bill was... [LAUGHS]
